import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 1.87

by A. L. Shmel'kin

Does every finitely generated matrix group have a finite basis of identities?
The problem refers back to Problem 1.86 and asks the same question for matrix
groups, at least over fields of characteristic zero.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«1.87»

/-- A word is an identity (law) of a group if every evaluation of its variables
in the group sends it to the identity element. -/
def IsIdentity (G : Type) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ w = 1

/-- A group has a finite basis of identities if its identity theory is the
semantic consequence closure of a finite set of group words. -/
def HasFiniteIdentityBasis (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), S.Finite ∧
    ∀ w : FreeGroup ℕ, IsIdentity G w ↔
      ∀ (H : Type) [Group H],
        (∀ v ∈ S, IsIdentity H v) → IsIdentity H w

/--
Does every finitely generated matrix group over a field have a finite basis of
identities? More precisely, for every field $K$, every $n$, and every finitely
generated subgroup $G \leq \operatorname{GL}_n(K)$, is the set of all group
laws of $G$ the consequence closure of a finite set of laws?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.87» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (n : ℕ)
      (G : Subgroup (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) K)),
      G.FG → HasFiniteIdentityBasis G := by
  sorry

/--
At least, does every finitely generated matrix group over a field of
characteristic zero have a finite basis of identities? More precisely, for
every characteristic-zero field $K$, every $n$, and every finitely generated
subgroup $G \leq \operatorname{GL}_n(K)$, is the set of all group laws of $G$
the consequence closure of a finite set of laws?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.87».variants.char_zero : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] [CharZero K] (n : ℕ)
      (G : Subgroup (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) K)),
      G.FG → HasFiniteIdentityBasis G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.87»

Consequence is modeled semantically: a word follows from a set of identities when every group satisfying that set also satisfies the word. Thus `HasFiniteIdentityBasis G` says that the complete identity theory of `G` is exactly the semantic consequence closure of a finite set. The defining biconditional also ensures that each member of the finite set is itself a law of `G`.

An `n`-dimensional matrix group over `K` is represented as a `Subgroup (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) K)`, and finite generation is expressed by Mathlib's `Subgroup.FG`. The quantification includes `n = 0`, as required by the decomposition's unrestricted `every n`; this only adds the trivial zero-dimensional general linear group.
The primary declaration quantifies over all Mathlib fields. The explicitly requested weaker variant uses the same statement with the additional typeclass assumption `CharZero K`.
Groups used in semantic consequence and fields/matrix groups are quantified in `Type`, matching the repository's standard small-universe convention for yes/no problems.

/-!
# Conjecture 1.87

by A. L. Shmel'kin

The same question for matrix groups (at least over a field of characteristic $0$).

"The same question" refers to Problem 1.86 (also by A. L. Shmel'kin): "Does every
finitely generated soluble group have a finite basis of identities?" So Problem 1.87 asks:
does every finitely generated matrix group, i.e. every finitely generated subgroup of
$\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ for a field $K$, have a finite basis of identities (at least when $K$
has characteristic $0$)?

An identity (law) of a group $G$ is a word $w$ in the free group on countably many letters
$x_0, x_1, \dots$ such that $w(g_0, g_1, \dots) = 1$ for all $g_0, g_1, \dots \in G$. A set
$B$ of identities of $G$ is a basis of the identities of $G$ if every identity of $G$ is a
consequence of $B$, i.e. holds in every group in which all the identities in $B$ hold.
Equivalently, the variety of groups generated by $G$ is defined by the laws in $B$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

universe u

namespace Kourovka.«1.87»

/-- A word $w$ in the free group on the countably many letters $x_0, x_1, \dots$ is a law
(identity) of the group $G$ if $w$ evaluates to $1$ under every substitution of elements of
$G$ for the letters, i.e. under every group homomorphism `FreeGroup ℕ →* G`. -/
def IsLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, f w = 1

/-- A word $w$ is a consequence of a set $B$ of words if $w$ is a law of every group in which
all the words of $B$ are laws. -/
def IsConsequence (B : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], (∀ b ∈ B, IsLaw H b) → IsLaw H w

/-- A group $G$ has a finite basis of identities if there is a finite set $B$ of laws of $G$
such that every law of $G$ is a consequence of $B$. -/
def HasFiniteBasisOfLaws (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ B : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ),
    (∀ w ∈ B, IsLaw G w) ∧ ∀ w, IsLaw G w → IsConsequence.{u} (B : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) w

/-- The trivial word is a law of every group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLaw_one (G : Type*) [Group G] : IsLaw G 1 := fun f => map_one f

/-- The commutator $[x_0, x_1]$ is a law of every commutative group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLaw_commutator_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] :
    IsLaw G ⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆ := fun f => by
  rw [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm, mul_comm]

/--
The same question (as Problem 1.86) for matrix groups: does every finitely generated
subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$, for a field $K$ and $n \geq 0$, have a finite basis of
identities? That is, is there a finite set of identities of $G$ from which all identities
of $G$ follow?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.87» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (n : ℕ) (G : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)),
      G.FG → HasFiniteBasisOfLaws G := by
  sorry

/--
The weaker form explicitly requested in the problem ("at least over a field of
characteristic $0$"): does every finitely generated subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$, for a
field $K$ of characteristic $0$ and $n \geq 0$, have a finite basis of identities?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]

    ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] [CharZero K] (n : ℕ) (G : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)),
      G.FG → HasFiniteBasisOfLaws G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.87»

    w ∈ laws G ↔ ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1 := by
  simp only [laws, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker]
  exact ⟨fun h f => h (FreeGroup.lift f),
    fun h φ => by simpa using h (FreeGroup.lift.symm φ)⟩

/-- The trivial group satisfies every identity. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem laws_unit : laws Unit = ⊤ :=
  eq_top_iff.2 fun _ _ => mem_laws_iff.2 fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- The free group on countably many generators satisfies no non-trivial identity. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem laws_freeGroup : laws (FreeGroup ℕ) = ⊥ :=
  eq_bot_iff.2 fun w hw => by
    simpa [FreeGroup.lift_of_apply] using mem_laws_iff.1 hw FreeGroup.of

/-- The verbal subgroup of `FreeGroup ℕ` determined by a set of words `S`: the subgroup
generated by all images of elements of `S` under endomorphisms of `FreeGroup ℕ`. Its
elements are exactly the consequences of the words in `S`, i.e. the words that are
identities of every group in which all words of `S` are identities. -/
def verbalSubgroup (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  Subgroup.closure {w | ∃ s ∈ S, ∃ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ, φ s = w}

/-- Every word in `S` is a consequence of `S`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem subset_verbalSubgroup (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : S ⊆ verbalSubgroup S :=
  fun s hs => Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨s, hs, MonoidHom.id _, rfl⟩

/-- The empty set of words has no non-trivial consequences. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_empty : verbalSubgroup ∅ = ⊥ := by
  simp [verbalSubgroup]

/-- Every word is a consequence of the identity `x_0 = 1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_of_zero : verbalSubgroup {FreeGroup.of 0} = ⊤ :=
  eq_top_iff.2 fun w _ =>
    Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨FreeGroup.of 0, rfl, FreeGroup.lift fun _ => w, by simp⟩

whose consequences are exactly the identities of `G`; equivalently, the variety of
groups generated by `G` is finitely based. -/
def HasFiniteBasisOfLaws (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ), verbalSubgroup ↑S = laws G

/-- The trivial group has a finite basis of identities, namely `{x_0}`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasFiniteBasisOfLaws_unit : HasFiniteBasisOfLaws Unit :=
  ⟨{FreeGroup.of 0}, by rw [laws_unit, Finset.coe_singleton, verbalSubgroup_of_zero]⟩

-/

    ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (n : ℕ) (G : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)),

/-!
# Conjecture 1.87

by A. L. Shmel'kin

Problem 1.86 asks whether every finitely generated soluble group has a finite
basis of identities. Problem 1.87 asks the same question for matrix groups, at
least over fields of characteristic zero.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«1.87»

/-- A word is an identity (law) of a group if it evaluates to the identity
element under every assignment of its variables. -/
def IsGroupIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- A group has a finite basis of identities if there is a finite set of its
identities from which every identity of the group is a semantic consequence.
Here semantic consequence means validity in every group satisfying every
identity in the basis. -/
def HasFiniteIdentityBasis (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ basis : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ),
    (∀ w ∈ basis, IsGroupIdentity G w) ∧
    ∀ w, IsGroupIdentity G w ↔
      ∀ (H : Type) [Group H],
        (∀ v ∈ basis, IsGroupIdentity H v) → IsGroupIdentity H w

/--
Does every finitely generated matrix group have a finite basis of identities?
Precisely, for every field $K$, every $n$, and every finitely generated subgroup
$G \leq \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$, does the variety generated by $G$ have a finite basis
of identities?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.87» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (n : ℕ) (G : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)),
      G.FG → HasFiniteIdentityBasis G := by
  sorry

/--
At least over a field of characteristic zero, does every finitely generated
matrix group have a finite basis of identities? Precisely, for every
characteristic-zero field $K$, every $n$, and every finitely generated subgroup
$G \leq \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$, does the variety generated by $G$ have a finite basis
of identities?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.87».variants.char_zero : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] [CharZero K] (n : ℕ) (G : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)),
      G.FG → HasFiniteIdentityBasis G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.87»
modeling_decisions: A matrix group is represented as a subgroup `G : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)`, with `G.FG` expressing the finite-generation hypothesis inherited from Problem 1.86.

A group identity is encoded by a word in `FreeGroup ℕ` that evaluates to `1` under every assignment of its variables. Countably many variable names represent every ordinary identity, since each word uses only finitely many variables.

Consequence is modeled semantically: a word follows from a basis when it is an identity of every group satisfying every basis identity. Thus `HasFiniteIdentityBasis G` says exactly that all identities of `G` are the semantic consequences of a finite subset of its identities.
The primary declaration quantifies over fields of arbitrary characteristic; the requested weaker variant adds `[CharZero K]`.
The dimension is quantified as `n : ℕ`, matching the decomposition. At `n = 0`, `GL (Fin 0) K` is trivial, a harmless boundary case.
